minutes.headline: Assessors approved June 3 minutes, heard MUNIS billing problems, and went into executive session on abatements.
minutes.summary: The board discussed recusal etiquette and warned against sharing executive session deliberations outside the room. The principal assessor reported on remaining abatements, the LA-19 equalized value and growth estimate, and MUNIS billing problems, including a consultant visit planned for the 17th. Minutes were approved, documents were signed, and the board entered executive session on abatement applications.

votes.motion: Accept the June 3rd minutes as modified.
Accept the executive session minutes as amended (June 3rd).
Accept the May 20th executive session minutes, with Mr rabbit recused.
Suspend open meeting and enter executive session under purpose 7 (c.59 s.60, abatement applications), not to return to open session.

budget_items.topic: LA-19 equalized value and estimated new growth
budget_items.what_was_said: Principal assessor explained the state uses equalized value and estimated growth to distribute state aid. She must tell the state soon if growth will not be met.
A consultant would assist with the billing process for a day, at a rate described as reasonable.
Board received a discount and a free second box of door hangers.
A member's conference registration was signed; hotel cost was discussed but the member will stay with family.
Board reviewed and signed abatement reports, including a large one.

decisions.decision: Recused members will be asked to leave the room during executive session in future.
Residents with specific questions will be encouraged to make an appointment to meet the board in executive session.
No special meeting needed for remaining abatements; next meetings set for July 22nd and August 19th.
Board will look at exemption Clause 18 and prepare an exemptions packet for the fall.

what_happened.line: The board entered executive session to take up abatement applications, after a vote whose result is not detailed in the minutes.
The board decided that no special meeting is needed for the remaining abatements and set its next meetings for July 22 and August 19.
The principal assessor reported on the LA-19 equalized value and estimated new growth, which the state uses to distribute state aid, and said the state must be told soon if growth will not be met.
The board discussed MUNIS billing problems and a one-day consultant to help with billing; no resolution was reached.
The board said it will look at the exemption Clause 18 and prepare an exemptions packet for the fall.

why_it_matters: The LA-19 growth estimate feeds how the state distributes aid, and a growth shortfall reported to the state can affect what the town can count on in its budget.
Unresolved MUNIS billing problems touch how and when tax and excise bills reach residents, and abatement decisions made in closed session decide individual bills.
An exemptions packet planned for the fall is relevant to residents who may qualify for a property tax exemption.
watch_next: Board of Assessors meetings on July 22 and August 19.
The MUNIS consultant visit planned for the 17th, and the exemptions packet due in the fall.
